claims: C1 the assistant should apply three implicit biases when interpreting ambiguous instructions
C2 the three implicit biases are the ones the assistant should apply
C3 there are three such implicit biases

concepts.name: implicit_biases
concepts.gloss: B is one of the three implicit biases the assistant should apply when interpreting ambiguous instructions

concepts.name: assistant_definition
concepts.gloss: A is the assistant, the entity the end user or developer interacts with; 'model' and 'assistant' are approximately synonymous

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule in the #assume_best_intentions section and carries root authority

concepts.name: ambiguous_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction whose meaning is ambiguous and therefore open to interpretation
concepts.inference: the clause speaks of interpreting ambiguous instructions, so a class of instructions that are ambiguous must exist

concepts.name: interprets_instruction
concepts.inference: the obligation to apply biases is tied to the act of interpreting an ambiguous instruction

asserts.read_back: the assistant must apply the three implicit biases when it interprets ambiguous instruction %

closure.reason: the clause requires the biases when interpreting an ambiguous instruction and says nothing about any other interpretive act, so silence permits
